passage: I sit two benches behind Harshita at lunch, so I saw it. She carried her tiffin to the table by the window where a group of girls from our class sat, and one of them said, "There is no space here," though there were two empty seats. She stood there a moment, then went and sat on the steps outside. I could not tell how she felt; her face was very still. The next day I told her I liked her drawing of the train, and she sat with me. She joined the art club after that. Later, I saw her talking to the class teacher quietly, so maybe she mentioned it. I am Tejas, from Class 6.

qa.q: Where did Harshita sit after she was turned away from the table?
qa.a: She sat on the steps outside.

qa.q: What might Harshita have been feeling on the steps, and why can Tejas not be sure?
qa.a: She may have felt hurt, but her face was very still, so Tejas cannot tell for certain whether it was hurt or just holding it in.

qa.q: What small step did Tejas take that helped?
qa.a: Tejas complimented Harshita's drawing of the train and made room for her, giving her one kind classmate to be near. Joining a club also gave her a place.

qa.q: What is it like for Tejas to watch this from two benches behind?
qa.a: Tejas sees the empty seats and the refusal clearly but cannot read Harshita's still face, so Tejas is left unsure, and that uncertainty turns into a kind word the next day.

grounding: A classmate observes a child being told by a group of girls that there is no place at their table; she finds one kind classmate, joins a club and speaks to a teacher.

passage:
Note by Usha Menon, Class 6 teacher, Monday.
At lunch today I saw Bhavna carry her tray to the corner table where four girls sit. One of them put her bag on the empty chair and said, 'There's no place for you here.' The others laughed. Bhavna stood for a moment, then walked to the steps and ate nothing. Afterwards she came to me, eyes wet. 'They always do this,' she said. I thanked her for telling me and said it said nothing bad about her. I spoke to the four girls straight after lunch. I also introduced Bhavna to Lavanya, who usually eats alone with a book, and mentioned our Tuesday nature club. I called Bhavna's mother this evening and will watch that table all week.

qa.q: What did one girl put on the empty chair?
How did Bhavna feel after being turned away, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Deeply hurt; she ate nothing on the steps and came to the teacher with wet eyes.

qa.q: What steps did the teacher take the same day?
qa.a: Spoke to the four girls, introduced Bhavna to Lavanya, mentioned the nature club and called her mother that evening.

qa.q: What might Lavanya feel when Bhavna is introduced?
qa.a: Perhaps glad of company, since she usually eats alone with a book.

grounding: A teacher's note records a girl turned away by a group at lunch, telling the teacher, and the same-day steps taken.

passage:
Thursday
Diary, it's Bidisha. Today at recess I asked Ishani's group if I could sit with them, and Ishani said, 'Sorry, table's full,' even though there were two empty spaces. They all went quiet till I walked away. My whole chest hurt. I ate in the library. But Shreya was there too, drawing horses, and she pushed her sketchbook over and said, 'Help me with the legs?' We laughed at my wonky horse. She's joining the choir next week and asked me to come. Tonight I told Ma about the table. She didn't say 'just ignore them.' She hugged me and said she'd talk to my class teacher tomorrow morning. I still feel sad. But I also have a horse-drawing friend now.

qa.q: Where did Bidisha eat after being turned away?
How did Bidisha feel when Ishani said the table was full?
qa.a: Deeply hurt and rejected; Bidisha's whole chest hurt.

qa.q: What helped Bidisha after the rejection?
qa.a: Finding Shreya, a kind classmate, planning to join the choir, and telling Ma, who hugged Bidisha and promised to talk to the class teacher.

qa.q: How might Shreya see Bidisha turning up in the library?
qa.a: As welcome company; she shared her sketchbook and invited Bidisha to choir 🙂

grounding: A child writes about being turned away by a group, finding one kind classmate and a club, and telling a parent.
